az_planetarium_the.blurb: The Planetarium is a steep, west-facing sport wall on West Twin Butte, on the edge of Sedona at roughly 4,500 feet. Fifteen routes are packed into one compact cliff, thirteen of them bolted and two traditional. The grades start at 5.10 and run up through a solid helping of 5.11 and 5.12, with a couple of 5.13s, so it suits strong climbers rather than beginners. Rock quality swings from poor to excellent depending on the line, so choose carefully. A short walk up a climbers' trail from the road puts you beneath the cave at the heart of the wall.

az_prow_area_the.blurb: The Prow Area is a small sport wall among the Black Mountains cliffs above Golden Valley, near Kingman, at about 3,500 feet. It holds fifteen bolted routes, which makes it one of the friendlier sectors in the zone: the grades begin at 5.5, cluster between 5.8 and 5.10, and top out at a single 5.11. The wall faces south to southeast. From the junction of the approach trail, take the left branch and follow the base of the cliff a short way. Good for a mixed group wanting steady moderate mileage on well-protected lines.

az_eastern_block.blurb: Eastern Block is a sport crag in the Black Mountains above Golden Valley, near Kingman, and the sister wall to the Prow. Around fifteen routes, nearly all bolted with one trad line, run from the 5.7s up to a few 5.11s, with most falling in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. It faces east-northeast, so expect sun early and shade as the day wears on. You can spot it from the base of the switchbacks by a long black stain streaking down the face, with a pair of big boulders sitting below. Take the right-hand branch where the approach trail forks.

az_mentor_cave.blurb: Mentor Cave is a steep sport cave on the shady south side of the Virgin River Gorge, beside the interstate in the Arizona Strip. Fifteen bolted routes pack the overhanging walls, and almost all are hard: most land between 5.11 and 5.13, with just one easy outlier. Lines are shorter than elsewhere in the gorge but notably more overhanging. Expect highway noise and a scrappy roadside setting, but also strong, sustained movement. A trail leads from the parking area under the freeway to the base, about ten minutes on foot. It is best in the cooler months.

az_hearthstone.blurb: Hearthstone is a big west-facing buttress in Bear Canyon on Mount Lemmon, above Tucson, standing opposite Chimney Rock along the Catalina Highway. The wall is steeper than the slabbier formation uphill from it. Fifteen routes are mostly traditional, with a few bolted lines, graded from easy 5.5 through to the 5.11 range, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. A cool, wooded canyon setting makes it a pleasant option when lower desert crags are warm. Reach it by dropping into the rocky drainage beside the buttress and following the streambed upstream.

az_acropolis.blurb: The Acropolis is a multipitch trad wall in Sabino Canyon on the Santa Catalina side of Tucson, built of gneiss. It sits directly above the Phoneline Trail and is easy to reach, with a short hike once the cliff comes into view. Fifteen traditional lines range from 5.5 to the 5.11 range, with the largest group at 5.10. Expect choss in places, with some lines cleaner than others, and an adventurous feel. The wider canyon is trad only, with no bolted routes. A good pick for confident leaders wanting a quiet day on a sizeable wall.

az_5_bee_cave.blurb: Bee Cave is one of the stronger sectors at the Dry in southern Arizona, a steep limestone cliff of roofs and faces. All fourteen routes are bolted, starting at 5.11 and mostly sitting in the 5.12s, with a couple harder. The first few bolts are easy, and the best rock begins about thirty feet up. It is among the first parts of the cliff to fall into shade, so it makes a handy place to start a day. A single trail with one big switchback leads in, and bees may visit the cave for water, so pants help.

az_eden.blurb: Eden is a secluded pocket of Christopher Creek Gorge, east of Payson, with walls rising on both sides of the creek and a waterfall-fed pool below. Fourteen routes, mainly sport with a little trad and one aid line, run from easy 5.7 up to 5.12, so there is something for most levels. The walk in is roughly half a mile from the car and finishes with a creek hop, so expect wet feet when the water is up. The gorge is hot in midsummer, with north-side walls sunny in winter and south-side walls shadier in warm months.
